title: GPU pool runway & burst playbook — notes
content:
Purpose: quick solo brain dump before the 1:1 and weekly capacity sync. Not polished — action items, numbers to verify, and an experiment plan for short bursts.

Context reminders:
- Dedicated pool: 48 A100s reserved across two regions (us-west2, eu-west1). Effective usable after host overhead ~ 44.
- Current monthly commit: 3.2k GPU-hours/month (contract ends Q2 renewal window).
- Average baseline consumption last 30d: 2.7k GPU-hours/month; peak weekly spikes up to ~3.6k.

Key questions I want answered in meetings:
- How conservative should runway be for PLs with heavy RLHF jobs? (TBD: ask product owners)
- Can finance amortize prepayment savings and show effective $/GPU-hour for dedicated vs on-demand?
- Is there appetite to convert 8 A100s to on-demand to increase burst headroom?

Quick runway calc (rough):
- Reserved capacity = 48 GPUs * 720 hours = 34,560 GPU-hours/month theoretical. But our contract only guarantees 3.2k GPU-hours/month? (note: mismatch — double-check: reserved pool is pooled across customers; need correct mapping)
- For our internal projects using reserved pool: baseline 2,700 / month. Buffer target = +20% = 3,240. Current commit covers baseline easily but not peak bursts.

Burst plan (experimental):
- Experiment name: BURST-omega (2-week window)
- Hypothesis: Adding short on-demand bursts during scheduled training windows reduces tail latency and lowers average cost per training job by improving GPU utilization efficiency.
- Config: allow autoscale to +8 GPUs (on-demand) for 3 windows/week (4h each) for 2 weeks. Track incremental cost and job completion time savings.
- Success metric: cost per training epoch down by >=10% OR mean job turnaround reduced by >=25% for the targeted job set.

Operational considerations / checklist for 1:1:
- Ask SRE: current preemption/retry behavior for on-demand burst nodes? (ticket?)
- Follow up with Release Eng: are there infra quotas we need to pre-raise for eu-west1?
- Confirm with Billing: show the effective blended $/GPU-hour for reserved vs burst slots (include egress/network assumptions).
- Verify autoscaler policies: min_idle, max_burst, cooldown settings. I think cooldown is 600s but need to confirm.

Notes to self: things to gather before sync:
- Pull 6 months of GPU-hour usage by team + daily 95th percentile consumption (sheet link above).
- List of top 10 jobs by GPU-hours and by tail latency.
- Tag jobs that are tolerant to preemption vs not.

Open design questions (brainstorm):
- Should we enforce a soft budget pool per team to prevent noisy neighbors consuming all reserved capacity during scheduled bursts?
- Could we expose a "reservation lease" concept to product teams: short-term reservations (4-72 hours) billed to team budgets, automatically converted to on-demand if unused?
- Pricing model: reveal per-team effective cost so teams can opt to reserve more if ROI > threshold.

Follow-ups / action items (owner -> due):
- Asha: run the BURST-omega experiment plan doc and put schedule in calendar (due: 2026-03-12).
- Diego: ask Billing for blended $/GPU-hour and deliver by next sync (due: 2026-03-09).
- Samir: verify autoscaler cooldown and submit infra quota request if needed (due: 2026-03-08).
- Me (reminder): scrub the reserved pool mapping — I misremembered the contract numbers; confirm actual reserved GPU-hour commit (due: 2026-03-06).

Meeting agenda draft (10 min prep):
- 5 min: current runway summary + major anomalies in last month
- 7 min: proposed BURST-omega experiment (config + success criteria)
- 5 min: ask for decision on temporary conversion of 8 GPUs to on-demand for bursts
- 3 min: assign followups and confirm owners

Potential blockers and mitigations:
- Blocker: finance needs formal approval to bill on-demand bursts to team budgets. Mitigation: provide cost modeling and small pilot cost cap.
- Blocker: infra quotas in eu-west1. Mitigation: pre-file ticket + ask for escalation during sync.

Random notes / crumbs to preserve:
- A few jobs seen last month had insane prefix cache inefficiency — consider profiling before granting burst capacity.
- Talk to Solutions Eng about customer-facing expectations for Dedicated customers during their planned bursts.

End. Keep this doc intentionally messy — I'll clean a runbook if BURST-omega looks promising.

Links referenced (short):
- usage sheet: https://drive.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1Zx_runway_forecast
- draft experiment checklist PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/reports/pull/2381
- jira epic: JIRA-ENG-4123
_notes_preview: personal brain dump for dedicated capacity 1:1s; includes runway math, experiment plan (BURST-omega), action items and things to verify with SRE/Billing/Release Eng.
